Subject: Realtime chat responses are timing out - FinLayer session 7891

Hi team,

We started seeing significant latency in the streaming chat for a subset of our users this afternoon. One session (session id 7891) had streaming responses pause for ~18s before a full response arrived; for other sessions tokens trickled in with 2–5s gaps. This is affecting our in-prod assistant and increased our customer SLA errors.

Attached is a short screenshot of the client timeline and a couple of request IDs we captured: r-0a3f, r-0a3g. The behavior appears to have started ~15:50 UTC and is intermittent — ~20% of requests in that window.

Can someone confirm if there are known issues on your side and advise a short-term mitigation? We can turn off streaming if needed, but that is a poor UX.

Thanks,
Alice

Hi Alice — thanks for the report and the request IDs. I’m escalating to our on-call and CS immediately.

Immediate steps we can take now (short-term):
- If you can tolerate slightly higher latency but consistent delivery, fallback to short-polling (poll interval 250ms) while we triage.
- If your client supports it, disable aggressive chunking (set chunk_threshold=0.2) — we’ve seen chunk boundaries amplify client-side stalls.
- Share 2–3 representative request_ids (you gave r-0a3f/r-0a3g; any more helps).

Laura / Ben — I’ve looped you in; please triage edge shard metrics and KV cache evictions for the timeframe 15:40–16:10 UTC. I’ll keep FinLayer updated on progress.

Hi Alice — Laura from Customer Success here. We're looking into this now. Quick triage notes and temporary mitigations you can apply while eng investigates: 

What to try immediately (client-side / config changes):
- Short-poll fallback: set streaming=false for the next 30–60 minutes and poll every 300ms. This turns the UX into slightly higher latency but prevents partial-token stalls.
- Retry window: increase client-side streaming read timeout to 30s to avoid premature aborts.
- Disable client-side backpressure: ensure your websocket receive buffer is not dropping frames (we've seen some SDK versions behave this way).

What we’ve requested from you:
1) Full HTTP trace for request_ids r-0a3f, r-0a3g and any other ids between 15:40–16:10.
2) Are you seeing the issue only on a single region/edge? If so which region did your clients connect to?

Attached: diag-requests-7891.tar.gz (logs + traces we can analyze). If you can upload the full traces we’ll correlate with our internal edge metrics.

We’ll provide an update within 90 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your users.

—Laura

Hi all — Ben on infra. Quick interim update and root-cause summary.

Timeline (short):
- 15:42–15:58 UTC (May 3): heightened scheduling activity on edge-shard-17 after a rolling autoscaler policy triggered kernel patch placement.
- During async kernel rollout a subset of replicas experienced aggressive KV cache compaction leading to frequent per-request prefix cache misses. Cache misses + kernel micro-pauses produced token emission gaps of 1–20s for affected requests.

Short-term mitigations we executed (done by 08:40 UTC May 4):
- Restored pre-rollback kernel on shard-17 (rollback completed at 07:30 UTC).
- Disabled the aggressive autoscaler policy for the shard and reprovisioned 3 extra warm replicas to absorb load.
- Applied a tenant pin to route FinLayer traffic away from the recovering replicas (this removed the majority of affected sessions).

Recommended immediate customer actions (we provided these to FinLayer and you can apply them if you want):
- If you need the fastest recovery today: switch to non-streaming polling for 60–180 minutes while we verify stability.
- If you keep streaming on: enable client read-timeout of 30s and add a client-side token-merge tolerance of 200ms to smooth UI.

Longer-term actions (we have tracked as INF-4127):
- Harden autoscaler rollback policy to avoid in-flight kernel replacements for hot shards.
- Add per-tenant circuit-breaker for streaming token emission gaps.
- Improve per-request KV cache metrics and alerting so we can surface these before customer-visible impact.

We have a postmortem doc with full traces and timelines — attaching the first-draft notes (postmortem-notes-7891.md) and linking the internal dashboard. If you’d like a joint review of the postmortem with your engineering team, we can schedule that this week.

Apologies again — we know this reduced UX quality. We’ll follow up with the final postmortem and code plan.

Ben Carter
Infra / On-call, Redwood Inference
